The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's own GitHub repository using a tagged release archive over HTTPS. The `source` array entry points to a predictable, versioned tarball (`v$pkgver.tar.gz`) hosted at the declared upstream URL. There are no command substitutions, remote code executions, or network requests outside of this declared source during the sourcing phase.

The `pkgver` function is not defined, so no dynamic version computation occurs. All variables are statically assigned, and there is no top-level executable code outside of variable declarations. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, so the downloaded source will be verified (though even if it were 'SKIP', that would not make this step unsafe, as noted in the instructions). No dangerous operations such as `curl | bash`, `eval`, or data exfiltration attempts are present in the global scope.

Since `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` only sources the PKGBUILD and downloads the sources—without running `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`—and since the global scope contains no malicious logic, this operation is safe.
</details>
